'''Marcus Terrell Thornton''' (born June 5, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]] before being selected in the second round of the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]]. He played eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[New Orleans Hornets]], [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Houston Rockets]] and [[Washington Wizards]].

==College career==
Thornton played two years at [[Kilgore College]], a junior college in [[Kilgore, Texas]]. As a freshman in 2005–06, he averaged 14.5 points while shooting at 65 percent from the field. He averaged 26.9 points in his second season at Kilgore in 2006–07, earning first-team Junior College All-American honors and MVP honors for Region XIV.<ref name=bio>{{cite web| title = Marcus Thornton Stats, Video, Bio, Profile | url = http://www.nba.com/playerfile/marcus_t_thornton/bio/ | access-date = December 8, 2015 | work = NBA.com}}</ref> He was inducted into the Kilgore College Athletics Hall of Fame in 2025.<ref>[https://kcrangernation.com/information/KC_Athletics_Hall_of_Fame "KC Athletics Hall of Fame"] kcrangernation.com.</ref>

Following his sophomore season, Thornton transferred to [[Louisiana State University]]. As a junior in 2007–08 playing for the Tigers, he averaged 19.6 points (second in the SEC) and shot 81.7 percent from the free-throw line, the second-best percentage in the conference. As a senior in 2008–09, he averaged 21.1 points, 5.5 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game, subsequently earning the 2009 [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]]. In two seasons at LSU, he finished with 1,347 points, 21st all-time and with a 20.4 scoring average, he ranked sixth all-time. He also finished eighth in school history with 168 three-pointers.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Hornets (2009–2011)===
Thornton was selected with the 43rd overall pick by the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]], but his rights were traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. On February 23, 2010, in a loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], he tied a Hornets' franchise record for points scored by a rookie (37), and set a franchise record for points in a quarter (23) and points off the bench (previous, 33, [[Dell Curry]]). His 37 points also tied for the third most points by an NBA rookie off the bench since the 1976–77 season. He was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team in 2009–10 after averaging 14.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 25.6 minutes per game in 73 games (started 17) with New Orleans. He also set a franchise rookie record with 117 three-pointers in a season.<ref name="bio" />

===Sacramento Kings (2011–2014)===
[[File:Marcus Thornton Kings.jpg|thumb|right|Thornton with the Kings in 2013]]
On February 23, 2011, Thornton was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Carl Landry]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Kings Acquire Marcus Thornton from the New Orleans Hornets in Exchange for Carl Landry | url = http://www.nba.com/kings/news/press_release_2011_02_23.html | date = February 23, 2011 | access-date = February 24, 2011 | work = NBA.com}}</ref> On March 14, 2011, he scored a career-high 42 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Marcus Thornton's career night helps Kings wax Warriors | url = https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310314023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160803221118/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310314023 | url-status = dead | archive-date = August 3, 2016 | date = March 14, 2011 | access-date = December 8, 2015 | work = ESPN.com}}</ref>

In the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]]-shortened [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]], Thornton averaged a team-leading 18.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 34.9 minutes in starting all 51 games he played in.<ref name="bio" />

On January 24, 2014, Thornton tied his career-high of 42 points in an overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Game Rewind: Pacers 116, Kings 111 (OT) | url = http://www.nba.com/pacers/rewind-pacers-kings-140124 | date = January 24, 2014 | access-date = December 8, 2015 | work = NBA.com}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2014)===
On February 19, 2014, Thornton was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Jason Terry]] and [[Reggie Evans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-acquire-marcus-thornton-sacramento|title=Nets Acquire Marcus Thornton from Sacramento|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2014|access-date=February 19, 2014}}</ref> His best game for the Nets came on March 9, as he scored 27 points in a win over the Kings.<ref>{{cite web| title = Marcus Thornton 2013-14 Game Log | url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thornma01/gamelog/2014/ | access-date = December 8, 2015 | work = Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2014–2015)===
On July 10, 2014, Thornton was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team deal involving the Nets and the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-complete-three-team-trade|title=Celtics Complete Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2014|access-date=July 10, 2014}}</ref> On December 7, he scored a season-high 21 points in the Celtics' 101–93 win over the Washington Wizards.<ref>{{cite web| title = Marcus Thornton 2014-15 Game Log | url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thornma01/gamelog/2015/ | access-date = December 8, 2015 | work = Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2015)===
On February 19, 2015, Thornton was traded, along with a 2016 first-round pick, to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-complete-deal-boston-thornton-draft-pick|title=Suns Complete Deal with Boston for Thornton, Draft Pick|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}}</ref> He completed the 2014–15 season with the Suns playing in just nine games. He did not manage game time in 18 of a possible 27 games with the Suns, largely thanks to an Achilles' tendon injury and being a non-rotation player on a non-playoff team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coro|first=Paul|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/04/10/phoenix-suns-marcus-thornton-learning-cut-playing-time/25616503/|title=Phoenix Suns' Marcus Thornton 'learning' from cut in playing time|work=AZCentral.com|date=April 10, 2015|access-date=December 8, 2015}}</ref>

Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 26, 2016|access-date=February 26, 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2016–2017)===
On March 9, 2016, Thornton signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/03/09/wizards-sign-marcus-thornton|title=WIZARDS SIGN MARCUS THORNTON|work=MonumentalSportsNetwork.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=July 28, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he made his debut with the Wizards in a 114–93 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], recording two points, one assist and one steal in 20 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/WASUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Mack scores career-high 27 as Jazz beat Wizards 114-93|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 12, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref>

On July 28, 2016, Thornton re-signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/07/28/wizards-re-sign-marcus-thornton|title=Wizards Re-Sign Marcus Thornton|work=MonumentalSportsNetwork.com|date=July 28, 2016|access-date=July 28, 2016|archive-date=August 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813041112/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/07/28/wizards-re-sign-marcus-thornton|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 22, 2017, Thornton was traded, along with [[Andrew Nicholson (basketball)|Andrew Nicholson]] and a 2017 first round draft pick, to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Bojan Bogdanović]] and [[Chris McCullough]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/02/22/brooklyn-nets-acquire-first-round-draft-pick-nicholson-thornton-from-washington|title=BROOKLYN NETS ACQUIRE FIRST ROUND DRAFT PICK, ANDREW NICHOLSON AND MARCUS THORNTON FROM WASHINGTON|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2017|access-date=February 22, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Nets the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/02/23/brooklyn-nets-waive-marcus-thornton|title=BROOKLYN NETS WAIVE MARCUS THORNTON|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}}</ref>

===Grand Rapids Drive (2017–2018)===
On December 13, 2017, Thornton was acquired by the [[Grand Rapids Drive]] of the [[NBA G League|G-League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA G League Transactions|url=http://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 13, 2017|date=December 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=We added 2 new players to our roster yesterday: Clemson University product KJ McDaniels and NBA vet Marcus Thornton!|url=https://twitter.com/grdrive/status/942097097863716865|website=Twitter.com|access-date=December 16, 2017|date=December 16, 2017}}</ref>

===Beijing Ducks (2018)===
On February 4, 2018, Thornton signed with the [[Beijing Ducks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|title=北京男篮官宣签前火箭后卫 曾获索大腿称号|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2018-02-04/doc-ifyreyvz9051818.shtml|language=zh|date=February 4, 2018}}</ref>

=== Return to the Drive (2018–2019) ===
On December 11, 2018, Thornton was reacquired by the [[Grand Rapids Drive]] of the [[NBA G League|G-League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=OFFICIAL: Drive have re-acquired @NBA vet Marcus Thornton (@OfficialMT23)! |url=https://twitter.com/grdrive/status/1072555391341527040|date=December 11, 2018|website=Grand Rapids Drive on Twitter|access-date=December 11, 2018}}</ref> On March 3, 2019, Thornton scored 42 points to go along with 5 rebounds, 4 assists and 4 blocks in a 102–97 win over the Maine Red Claws.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021800361/|title=Grand Rapids Drive 102 Maine Red Claws 97|publisher=G-League Stats|date=March 3, 2019|access-date=January 10, 2020}}</ref>

===Motor City Cruise (2022)===
On January 8, 2022, Thornton was acquired via available player pool by the [[Motor City Cruise]] of the [[NBA G League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 8, 2022|access-date=January 8, 2022}}</ref> but was waived on January 21, after appearing in only 4 games.On February 18, 2025, Thornton was announced by Greek club Lavrio of the A1 division

==Personal life==
Thornton's fiancée, Lyndsey Duplessis, gave birth to their first child on January 1, 2016, a daughter named Maleia.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160102/HOUSAS/gameinfo.html |title=Duncan scoreless for 1st time but Spurs beat Rockets 121-103 |work=NBA.com |date=January 2, 2016 |access-date=January 3, 2016}}</ref> Thornton is a cousin of former NBA player [[Al Thornton]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wdsu.com/r/19863779/detail.html |title=Hornets Take UCLA's Collison, Trade For LSU's Thornton |work=WDSU.com |date=June 25, 2009 |access-date=December 8, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405194119/http://www.wdsu.com/r/19863779/detail.html |archive-date=April 5, 2012 }}</ref>
